FORM 4
 HISTORY PAPER 1 - MARKING SCHEME
 SECTION A.
 1. Define the term pre-history. (1 mark)
 • It is study of human activities before the invention of writing. /Study of unrecorded
 past human activities. (1x1=1mark)
 2. State two ways in which the migration of the Cushites into Kenya affected the
 Agikuyu during the pre-colonial period. (2 marks)
 i. They adopted female circumcision
 ii. They adopted the taboo against eating fish
 iii. There was conflict between them
 iv. They traded with each other
 v. They adopted the age-set system. (2x1=2marks)
 3. Identify the main economic activity of the Maasai during the pre-colonial period. (1
 mark)
 • Livestock keeping/pastoralism. (1x1=1mark)
 4. Give one way in which the translation of the bible into vernacular languages
 facilitated the spread of Christianity. (1 mark)
 i. The local people could read the bible
 ii. It created better understanding of the teaching of the bible.
 iii. More Africans could identify themselves with Christianity. (1x1=1mark)
 5. Apart from fort Jesus which other historical monument was built by the Portuguese
 in Kenya. (1 mark)
 • Vasco da Gama Pillar (in Malindi). (1x1=1 mark)
 6. Identify two communities which resisted the British occupation of Kenya. (2 marks)
 i. Agiriama
 ii. Bukusu
 iii. Somali
 iv. Nandi (any 2x1=2 marks)
 7. Name two groups which were involved in the provision of education services in
 Kenya during the colonial period. (2 marks)
 i. Christian missionaries
 ii. Colonial government
 iii. Asians/Indians but not the Arabs
 iv. Africans (any 2x1=2marks)
 8. State one type of democracy. (1 marks)
 i. Direct/pure
 ii. Indirect/impure
 iii. Constitutional/liberal
 9. Name the political party that led Kenya to independence. (1 mark)
 • The Kenya National African Union. (KANU)
 10. Identify two types of land ownership in Kenya. (2 marks)
 i. Public land
 ii. Community land
 iii. Private land (2x1=2marks)
 11. Highlight two national days celebrated in Kenya. (2 marks)
 i. Madaraka Day
 ii. Mashujaa
 iii. Jamhuri (any 2x1=2marks)
 12. Identify the type of constitution that is used in Kenya. (1 mark)
 • Written. (1x1=1mark)
 13. Outline two types of cases which are determined by the Kadhis court in Kenya. (2
 marks)
 i. Marriage cases
 ii. Divorce cases
 iii. Inheritance cases
 iv. Personal status (2x1=2marks)
 14. Highlight the main contribution of Wangari Maathai to the development of Kenya.
 (1 marks)
 • Environmental conservation/tree planting
 15. State two ways in which the Harambee spirit promotes national unity in Kenya. (2
 marks)
 i. It encourages people to work together
 ii. It promotes cooperation
 iii. It promotes equity in the distribution of resources
 iv. Enhances interaction of the people
 v. Promotes patriotism. (Any 2x1=2marks)
 16. Outline the main grievance of the Ukamba Member Association against the colonial
 government in Kenya. (1 mark)
 • The destocking policy (1x1=1mark)
 17. State two ways in which the national government of Kenya spends its recurrent
 expenditure. (2 marks)
 i. It establishes/maintains security organs
 ii. It pays salaries for state/public officers
 iii. It services domestic/foreign debts
 iv. It maintains foreign embassies
 v. It provides for social services/health care/education/cash transfer to the elderly
 vi. It caters for emergencies
 vii. Contributes to international organizations COMESA, UNO, AU, EAC
 viii. It repairs/maintains infrastructure. (2x1=2marks)
 SECTION B:
 Instructions: answer three questions in this section. (45 MARKS)
 18.
 a. State five causes of migration of the highland Nilotes in to Kenya during the
 pre-colonial period. (5 marks)
 i. There was outbreak of diseases/epidemics
 ii. There was population pressure
 iii. Due to their love for adventure/spirit of adventure/curiosity
 iv. Due to natural calamities/drought/famine
 v. They were searching for land for cultivation
 vi. They were running away from hostile neighbors/external attacks.
 vii. Due to internal conflicts/family feuds
 viii. They were searching for pasture/water. (Any
 5x1=5marks)
 b. Describe the political organization of the Luo during the pre-colonial period.
 (10 marks)
 i. The family was the lowest unit and its head was the father who was
 referred to as jaduong’
 ii. Several related families formed a clan
 iii. There were lineage council (Buch dhoot) which settled domestic issues
 iv. A council of elders existed in the clan/doho which was responsible for
 settling interfamily disputes
 v. Clans were grouped to form oganda headed by a chief elder (Routh)
 vi. There existed a council of elders (Buch piny) which comprised or
 representatives from each clan and mainly settled interclan disputes.
 vii. There was a class of warriors (thuondi) headed by a war leader (osumba
 mrwayi) and its main function was defend the community
 viii. The Luo was a decentralized community as they did not have an overall
 leader.
 ix. Religious leaders influenced politics. (Any 6x2= 12
 marks)
 19.
 a. Give three reasons why early visitors came to the Kenyan coast before
 1500AD. (3 marks)
 i. They wanted to participate in trade/control the commercial activities along
 the coast.
 ii. Some came as political/religious refugees
 iii. Some came as explorers/wanted to find out about the resources along the
 coast
 iv. They wanted ton spread their religion
 v. They wanted to establish settlements along the coast.
 (Any 3x1=3marks)
 b. Explain six effects of Christian missionary activities in Kenya. (12 marks)
 i. African culture/practices like polygamy changed with Africans adopting
 monogamy
 ii. Western civilization/education spread opening up schools which were
 centers for the spread of western education.
 iii. Christianity spread broadly resulting into some Africans abandoning their
 traditional religious beliefs/practices
 iv. They built hospitals/dispensaries which ensured provision of education.
 v. Mission education created jobs among the educated thus creating a
 gap/major difference between the literate and the illiterate
 vi. They led to formation of independent churches and schools to
 accommodate Africans whose children could not be admitted / accepted in
 mission school
 vii. They led to abolition of slave trade/establishment of centers such as frere
 town near Mombasa
 viii. They promoted exploration of east Africa as they discovered mountains,
 lakes/drew maps of the region which assisted late explorers
 ix. They contributed to the promotion of imperialism as missionaries opened
 the way for the colonialists to come and rule Kenya/flag followed the
 cross
 x. African representation was boosted as missionaries were allowed to
 represent their interests in the legco/Devonshire white paper of 1923
 xi. Translated the bible into local languages
 xii. They wrote the first Kiswahili dictionary/grammar book.
 xiii. They resulted to development of agricultural/technical skills by training
 Africans in industrial skills/introduced new farming methods
 (any 6 well explained x2 =12 marks)
 20.
 a. Identify five roles of chiefs during the colonial period in Kenya. (5 marks)
 i. Maintenance of public order
 ii. Hearing petty cases
 iii. Collecting taxes
 iv. To control the brewing of illegal liquor/cultivation of poisonous
 plants/carrying weapons
 v. Recruitment of labor. (5x1=5 marks)
 b. Explain five factors which led to the migration of Africans to the urban area
 in Kenya during the colonial period. (10 marks)
 i. The overcrowded/unproductive reserves created by the colonial
 government made living conditions made the living conditions
 difficult/unbearable thereby resulting into migrations to towns
 ii. Availability of better social services/amenities/health centers/education
 provided in towns attracted them.
 iii. The taxes imposed on Africans forced them to migrate to towns in search
 for jobs.
 iv. Availability of infrastructure/piped water/paved roads /electricity attracted
 many people to towns as they hoped for a better life
 v. Employment/job opportunities attracted people to towns as it promised
 them better wages
 vi. Mistreatment/frustration by the forced labor/public works forced them to
 move to towns
 vii. The widespread poverty in the rural/reserves caused them untold
 sufferings thereby making them to mi8grate to towns
 viii. Loss of land/landlessness caused by the colonial land policies resulted into
 a state of despair thereby forcing people to move to towns
 ix. African entrepreneurs wanted to take advantage of markets in the towns.
 (5x2=10 marks)
 21.
 a. Identify five methods used by the colonial government to discourage the
 activities of the Mau Mau Movement in Kenya. (5 marks)
 i. Many people were arrested /detained in various camps
 ii. The armed forces were used to suppress the movement/punitive
 expeditions
 iii. They killed/executed the activists
 iv. They used traitors or spies to reveal hiding grounds of the fighter
 v. The activists’ houses were destroyed/looted /villages burnt down
 vi. The people were put into concentration camps to curtail their movement
 vii. Kenya African union (KAU) was banned
 viii. The independent schools were closed down
 ix. The state of emergency was declared/ curfew enforced
 x. The government tortured MAU MAU supporters. (5x1=5marks)
 b. Explain five reasons why Mau Mau movement was able to last for a long
 time. (10 marks)
 i. Oathing united people and this made them to be committed to the course
 ii. Fighters used guerrilla warfare which made it difficult for the government
 to contain the rebellion
 iii. The civilian population sustained the rebellion by supplying food weapons
 and information
 iv. The movement was led by able leaders
 v. The abadares and Mount Kenya forest provided good hideouts for the
 MAU MAU fighters
 vi. Fighters had adequate weapons which enabled them to persist /continue
 fighting
 vii. The fighter were ex-service men and were therefore able to apply the
 military experience they had gained in WW1 and WW2
 viii. The movement received moral and material support from independent
 African countries. (5x 2= 10marks)
 SECTION C
 Instructions: answer any two questions from this section. (30 MARKS)
 22.
 a. Identify five elective positions in a general election in Kenya. (5 marks)
 i. President
 ii. Member of national assembly
 iii. Senator
 iv. Governor
 v. County women representative
 vi. Member of county assembly. (5x1=5marks)
 b. Describe the rights of an accused person in a court of law during trial in
 Kenya. (10 marks)
 i. The accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty
 ii. He/she should be informed of the charge with sufficient details so as to
 prepare a defense
 iii. One should be given adequate time to consult with the advocate/witness
 iv. One should be present when the court proceedings are taking place
 v. One should be given a chance to plead for leniency
 vi. One should not be forced to give evidence
 vii. One should be allowed to be heard
 viii. One should be allowed to appeal against the ruling
 ix. Right to legal representation
 x. To have the trial begin and concluded with few delay
 xi. To remain silent/ not to testify during the proceeding
 xii. To have the assistance on an interpreter if the accused person cannot
 understand language used in the trial. (5x2=10 marks)
 23.
 a. Give three categories of the Kenya Defense Forces. (3 marks)
 i. The Kenya army
 ii. The Kenya air force
 iii. The Kenya navy. (3x1=3marks)
 b. Explain six challenges encountered by the Kenya Police Service in the course
 of discharging their duties. (12 marks)
 i. Lack of support/negative attitude from the members of the public who
 refuse/withhold useful information.
 ii. Corruption among some officers renders them ineffective in discharging
 their duties.
 iii. Inadequate transport facilities hamper their movement thereby making it
 difficult for the to respond to emergencies.
 iv. Sophisticated weapons used by criminals threatens/endangers police
 officers’ lives.
 v. Inadequate modern communication equipment makes it difficult for them
 to relay/pass confidential information.
 vi. Interreference by politicians /members of the public demoralizes/frustrates
 their efforts.
 vii. Betrayal by some officers who collude with the criminals to break the
 law/subvert justice
 viii. Inadequate training of the officers renders them incompetent in
 discharging their duties/recruitment of officers with low academic
 qualifications.
 ix. Terrorism /increased acts of crime
 x. Poor working and living conditions e.g., poor housing/low salaries. (6x2-
 =12marks)
 24.
 a. State three roles of the Commission of Revenue Allocation (C.R.A). (3 marks)
 i. Making recommendations concerning basis for equitable sharing of
 resources
 ii. Making recommendations on matters concerning of/financial management
 by county governments
 iii. To define/enhance the revenue sources of the county and national
 government.
 iv. To encourage fiscal/financial responsibility/accountability
 v. To determine /publish/regularly review a policy which sets out criteria of
 identifying the marginalized areas
 vi. Revenue sharing between national and county government
 vii. Sharing revenue among county government. (3x1=3marks)
 b. Discuss six reasons why national government of Kenya prepares a budget
 annually. (12 marks)
 i. It enables the government to source for revenue to finance its activities
 /programs
 ii. To enable prudent use of resources/avoid waste
 iii. It enables the government to prioritize development according to the needs
 of the country
 iv. It creates confidence among donors/foreign countries/world bank/IMF
 who bridge budget deficits.\
 v. If helps the government to asses its performance based on set development
 targets/previous year’s performance.
 vi. It enhances accountability /transparency of the government in the eyes of
 the public/through the parliamentary watchdog committee
 vii. It enhances balance in the country’s revenue and expenditure hence
 avoiding budget deficits.
 viii. To enable the government, explain to the public the tax structure /set tax
 levels
 ix. The government is able to set aside some funds to be used in case of
 emergence in the course of the financial year.
 x. To ensure equitable share of resources/balanced development.
 (6x2=12 marks)
